title: Has Life in North Korea Changed Since 2013?
gist: A very thin teaser (123 words) promoting Jerome Sauvage's memoir 'Witness to North Korea', drawn from his three years as UN Resident Coordinator in the DPRK, and posing but not yet answering whether early-2010s ground experience still describes today's North Korea. Substantive analysis is behind the cutoff; the extractable signal is the framing question and the practitioner-level view of DPRK engagement.

themes.theme: Relevance of Pre-2013 DPRK Ground Experience

insights.claim: Whether a memoir of UN humanitarian and diplomatic work in the DPRK in the early 2010s still describes North Korea today is treated as a genuinely open question by North Korea specialists including the Wall Street Journal's Beijing bureau chief Jonathan Cheng and NK News' Alannah Hill.
insights.speaker: Jerome Sauvage
insights.so_what: Analysts relying on pre-COVID DPRK field reporting should treat their priors as potentially stale; direct-observation data on North Korea is scarce and aging.
insights.locator: Last month, as I launched my new book

insights.claim: Understanding engagement with the DPRK requires the granular, often maddening reality of day-to-day diplomacy and humanitarian work rather than the abstract language of policy briefs.
insights.speaker: Jerome Sauvage
insights.so_what: Operational friction, not declared policy, determines what any North Korea deal or aid channel can actually deliver — discount headline agreements accordingly.
insights.quote: what it actually means to engage with the DPRK – not in the abstract language of policy briefs, but through the granular, often maddening, reality of day-to-day diplomacy and humanitarian work
insights.locator: I wrote this book for anyone wishing to understand
